title: complete Maven Central registration process
body: @participant1 as you mentioned in [my PR](https://github.com/participant1/whisper.cpp/pull/944#issuecomment-1696075240) you still need to create an empty GitHub repository `OSSRH-94491` before we can publish the Java library.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Yup, created it a few days ago: https://github.com/participant1/OSSRH-94491

I also set the issue status to Open. The secrets are in place. Should be good now

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
The jar file needs to be signed before it can be published.

https://<redacted-host>/8.1/userguide/signing_plugin.html#sec:signatory_credentials

You will need to define project secrets:

GPG_PASSPHRASE
GPG_PRIVATE_KEY

![image](https://github.com/participant1/whisper.cpp/assets/1866161/4d0e46e5-ed71-4bde-8d4a-37b98ed8fc89)

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I think there's something wrong with the `JIRA_USER` and/or `JIRA_PASS`. I get exactly the same error below when I set either to the wrong value.

> Could not PUT 'https://<redacted-host>/service/local/staging/deploy/maven2/io/github/participant1/whispercpp/1.4.0/whispercpp-1.4.0.jar'. Received status code 401 from server: Unauthorized

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
I think I've got those wrong last time. Should be good now.
Set `JIRA_USER` and `JIRA_PASS` to my https://<redacted-host>/login.jsp login account

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant1 can you try generating the `PGP_SECRET` again using `gpg --armor --export` (or maybe `gpg --export-secret-keys -a -o secret-key.asc`)

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
I tried generating a new `PGP_SECRET` and re-runing the java workflow from master but it still fails.

![image](https://github.com/participant1/whisper.cpp/assets/1991296/a9c3c919-4003-4dae-9771-2858d73f30ee)

We currently have the following secrets:

![image](https://github.com/participant1/whisper.cpp/assets/1991296/16d8011d-2cea-4f7c-8385-0281c26c4000)

- `GPG_PRIVATE_KEY` and `GPG_PASSPHRASE` are my Github signing key data
- the `PGP_SECRET` I just generated a few minutes ago with the `gpg` command

Regarding the `PGP_SECRET` and `GPG_PRIVATE_KEY`, I'm not sure if they should include the ASCII prefix and suffix.
For example, the output of `gpg --armor --export` looks like this:

```
-----BEGIN PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----

[base64]
-----END PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----
```

Do I set the secret to be equal to just `[base64]` or also include the prefix and suffix?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: I think inlcude the `-----BEGIN PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK-----` and end block

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Updated `PGP_SECRET` to include it

I think ~`GPG_PASSPHRASE`~ `GPG_PRIVATE_KEY` also includes it, but AFAICT it is not used by the workflow anyway.

What about `PGP_PASSPHRASE`:

https://github.com/participant1/whisper.cpp/blob/1d3e6683e6442cc0135a90b668b41e979c4440ed/.github/workflows/build.yml#L436-L442

I suppose it is optional, but I can also create an empty secret

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Let's try using secrets.GPG_PRIVATE_KEY and GPG_PASSPHRASE

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Should work now when we merge #1267.

comments.body: Thank you! Should I remove the `PGP_SECRET` secret?
